questions.text: Which improvement model uses the Plan-Do-Study-Act cycle?
questions.explanation: The Model for Improvement, developed by Associates in Process Improvement and popularized by IHI, uses the PDSA cycle.

questions.text: In the DMAIC process improvement framework, what does the 'M' stand for?
questions.explanation: DMAIC stands for Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control — a Six Sigma improvement framework.

questions.text: A Pareto chart is used to:

options.b: Identify the most frequent causes of a problem
options.d: Map the steps in a process

questions.explanation: A Pareto chart displays causes in descending frequency, helping teams focus on the 'vital few' causes that account for most problems (80/20 rule).

questions.text: Which of the following tools is BEST suited for identifying variation and determining if a process is in statistical control?
questions.explanation: Control charts plot process data over time with upper and lower control limits to detect special cause variation.
Lean is focused on identifying and eliminating waste (non-value-added activities) to improve efficiency and flow.

questions.text: A process map or flowchart is MOST useful for:

options.b: Visualizing the steps and decision points in a process
options.c: Calculating standard deviation of process data

questions.explanation: Flowcharts visually represent the sequence of steps, decisions, and handoffs in a process, making them useful for identifying inefficiencies.

questions.text: In a cause-and-effect analysis, the 'bones' of a fishbone diagram typically represent:

options.c: Categories of potential causes such as people, process, equipment, and environment

questions.explanation: The 'bones' represent major categories of causes (often the 6 Ms: Man, Machine, Method, Material, Measurement, Mother Nature).

questions.text: Which of the following BEST describes 'common cause variation'?

options.a: Variation caused by a specific, identifiable event
options.b: Variation inherent in the process that is predictable and consistent
options.d: Variation that requires immediate corrective action

questions.explanation: Common cause (or random) variation is inherent in any process. It is predictable within a range and does not require special investigation.

questions.text: Before beginning a process improvement project, a quality team should FIRST:

options.a: Implement a solution based on best practices
options.b: Clearly define the problem and establish a baseline measure
options.c: Survey all staff involved in the process
options.d: Review benchmarking data from peer organizations

questions.explanation: Defining the problem clearly and establishing a baseline allows the team to measure whether any intervention produces improvement.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key principle of the 'Five Whys' technique?

options.a: Asking 'why' five times to identify the root cause of a problem
options.b: Involving five stakeholders in each improvement meeting
options.c: Completing five PDSA cycles before implementing a change
options.d: Identifying five process improvement opportunities per quarter

questions.explanation: The Five Whys technique repeatedly asks 'why' to drill down past symptoms to the underlying root cause of a problem.

questions.text: A hospital reduces medication errors by 40% after implementing a barcode scanning system. This is an example of which type of improvement strategy?
questions.explanation: Barcode scanning forces verification before medication administration, making errors harder to commit — this is an error-proofing or poka-yoke strategy.

questions.text: Which term describes the 'voice of the customer' in quality improvement?

options.c: The needs, expectations, and preferences of patients and stakeholders

questions.explanation: Voice of the Customer (VOC) captures the needs, expectations, and preferences of patients and other stakeholders to drive improvement.

questions.text: A 'quick win' in process improvement refers to:

options.a: A change that is implemented without testing
options.b: A small, low-effort improvement that produces rapid visible results
options.c: A large-scale transformation completed in under 30 days
options.d: A solution adopted directly from another organization

questions.explanation: Quick wins build momentum and stakeholder confidence by delivering visible improvements early in an improvement initiative.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST describes the 'Improve' phase in DMAIC?

options.d: Monitoring the process to ensure gains are sustained

questions.explanation: In the Improve phase, teams generate potential solutions, pilot test them, and implement the ones that address the verified root causes.

questions.text: A scatter diagram is used to show:

options.a: The frequency distribution of a single variable
options.b: The relationship or correlation between two variables

questions.explanation: Scatter diagrams plot two variables against each other to visually display whether a relationship or correlation exists.
